title: AWS CEO Says AI Spending Isn’t a Bubble Just Yet — Amazon’s Cloud Chief Says ‘We Feel Really Good’ as Ray
key_facts: AWS CEO Matt Garman said on an Andreessen Horowitz podcast: 'We feel really good about the spend we're making now.'
He said AWS takes a diversified approach, so not all capacity is tied to one customer.
The majority of AWS usage today is core compute, storage and inference, workloads that 'just aren't gonna go away'.
He compared AI start-ups to the venture model: not every billion-dollar start-up will make it, as with the internet bubble.
AWS exited the second quarter with a backlog of nearly $500 billion.
Yahoo notes AI bubble talk is rising as several chip stocks hit record highs and as Ray Dalio warned this week that AI speculation may be near its peak.
quote_evidence: "We feel really good about the spend we're making now," Garman said in a new podcast posted on the YouTube page of venture capital outfit Andreessen Horowitz.
"Those are the workloads that just aren't gonna go away."
"There was a bubble, a bunch of internet companies didn't make it, and the internet's still a thing."
why_it_matters_hint: A cloud-industry insider answers bubble fears, but it is a company executive defending his own spending.
event_date: 9 Oct 2026 (Yahoo article); podcast date not stated
